answer.summary: Criteria drift is the way people’s standards for good and bad outputs evolve as they inspect real model outputs: they uncover expectations and failure modes they could not have specified beforehand, even when they are experts.

sections.content: You can’t fully define evaluation rubrics upfront. As people review more outputs, their views of what counts as good or bad change, and they notice new failure modes they had not anticipated—sometimes only after seeing around 10 outputs. Shreya says this happened even with experienced developers. She also notes that reviewing data reveals additional product expectations that then get added to the judge prompt, so the criteria need to remain flexible and evolve.
